look_here_first: FIRST measure the flower pedicel from its base to the calyx on several blooms: typically very short, about 1.6–3.2 mm in regional accounts. Inspect the calyx side-on for conspicuous lobes, and check lower leaves for occasional three-parted blades. Do not identify by purple flowers or branch angle.

best_field_traits: Green hemiparasitic herb with narrow simple leaves and tubular bilaterally symmetric flowers.
Flower pedicels very short in regional descriptions (about 1.6–3.2 mm); verify at several flowers.
Calyx lobes conspicuous relative to those of A. edwardsiana.

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. edwardsiana generally bears longer flower pedicels (to ~30 mm) and much shorter calyx lobes. A. heterophylla usually has very short pedicels and conspicuous calyx lobes; occasionally three-cleft lower leaves. Narrow leaves, right-angle branching and pink flowers overlap. Other Agalinis must be keyed from intact calyx and pedicel measurements; do not use flower color alone.
